question:
A 33-year-old male presents to the office with low back pain that began 2 days ago after starting a new
weightlifting routine at the gym. He describes the pain as sharp and nonradiating. His medical history is
unremarkable. On examination, there is localized tenderness and warmth over the right lumbar
paraspinal muscles. Structural evaluation of the lumbar spine reveals a posterior right transverse
process at L3, which becomes less prominent when he bends backward. The remainder of the lumbar
spine shows no movement restrictions. What is the most appropriate positioning to treat this patient’s
lumbar somatic dysfunction using high velocity, low amplitude (HVLA) technique? Answer Choices: (A)
Right lateral recumbent, inferior arm pulled caudad (B) Supine, torso flexed and sidebent left (C)
Supine, torso rotated right and sidebent left (D) Left lateral recumbent, torso extended and rotated right
(E) Left lateral recumbent, inferior arm pulled anteriorly (F) Prone, torso rotated left with lumbar
extension (G) Right lateral recumbent, torso flexed and rotated left (H) Left lateral recumbent, inferior
arm pulled cephalad (I) Right lateral recumbent, torso extended and rotated left (J) Left lateral
recumbent, inferior arm pulled caudad
 A. Left lateral recumbent, torso extended and rotated right
B. Left lateral recumbent, inferior arm pulled cephalad
C. Left lateral recumbent, inferior arm pulled anteriorly

D. Right lateral recumbent, torso extended and rotated left
E. Left lateral recumbent, inferior arm pulled caudad
F. Right lateral recumbent, inferior arm pulled caudad
G. Prone, torso rotated left with lumbar extension
H. Right lateral recumbent, torso flexed and rotated left
I. Supine, torso rotated right and sidebent left
J. Supine, torso flexed and sidebent left
